name: Barbie Pink
lede: Barbie Pink is a vivid magenta-pink linked to Mattel's Barbie doll brand, a deep purplish pink by the 1955 ISCC-NBS standard even though the brand name itself only spread widely decades later.

sections.title: A brand name for a vivid pink
sections.body:
Our data carries this as a manual override tied to Mattel's Barbie brand pink, filed by ISCC-NBS in 1955 as a deep purplish pink, about 6.9 units from the historical reference, with Munsell notation 4.7RP 5.9/18.0 [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary records a close match first appearing in 1926, at plate 6, swatch K5, decades before the Barbie doll itself existed (Mattel introduced Barbie in 1959) [1]. The 2010 xkcd crowd survey later gave the same stretch of pink its own popular vote [1].

Google's Ngram data shows the phrase "barbie pink" barely used before 1990, rising through the 2000s and peaking around 2010 [1]. The closest look-alike in our data is [[persian-rose|Persian Rose]], 3.0 units away and more vivid, with [[french-fuchsia|French Fuchsia]] close too and [[hot-pink|Hot Pink]] a duller, lighter neighbor [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, within a CIEDE2000 difference of 4, as photographed [2]. A color this saturated and this tied to twentieth-century plastics has no real counterpart in historical pigments, which is exactly what the absence shows [2].

questions.q: Which 1955 standard first filed the swatch now called Barbie Pink, as a deep purplish pink?
True or false: the phrase "barbie pink" was common in print well before Mattel's Barbie doll existed.

openers: Barbie Pink's underlying swatch was filed by ISCC-NBS in 1955, four years before Mattel's Barbie doll existed at all.
